question: Select the option that has an error in the usage of the present perfect tense.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence "**Reh has complete his homework**", the verb "**complete**" is incorrectly used.
 
• The present perfect tense requires the past participle form of the verb, not the base form. The correct form of the verb is "**completed**".
 
• Thus, the correct sentence should be: "**Reh has completed his homework**."
 
• Other options are grammatically correct and appropriately use the present perfect tense with the correct form of the verb: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** "I have completed my task" – correct usage of the present perfect tense.
 
• **Option 2:** "Ram has completed his project" – correct usage of the present perfect tense.
 
• **Option 4:** "Rashi has completed her homework" – correct usage of the present perfect tense.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Reh has **completed** his homework."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Tense** uses the auxiliary verb "**has/have**" with the **past participle** form of the main verb (e.g., completed, finished, eaten).
 
• The past participle of "complete" is "**completed**," not "complete".
